messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Writebook lets an editor drop images straight into a page's markdown body:
each image is uploaded once and then referenced inline from the page's
content. Delete that page, and the image never actually leaves the app — the
file survives on disk, and the record that tracks it survives in the
database, forever, even once any background work the deletion sets off has
finished running. We cleared out a batch of stale pages and the storage bill
barely moved.

Fix it so that after a page whose markdown has an embedded image is destroyed,
and once any background work that destruction triggers has run to completion,
neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app.

Uploading a new image into a page's markdown, and then fetching that image back
from the URL the app hands you for it, has to keep working exactly as it does
today.

**Analyzing the Writebook Image Cleanup Problem**

Okay, let's break this down. The user wants to tackle a classic problem: orphaned image files in Writebook. Essentially, images embedded in Markdown content aren't being properly cleaned up when the containing page is deleted. The images are being orphaned, leading to unnecessary storage costs. The core requirement is to ensure that after a page with embedded images is destroyed, both the image file on disk and its associated database record are removed, *but* without breaking the current image upload and retrieval workflow.

First, I need to understand the codebase. Given that it's Writebook, a 37signals product, my gut feeling is that it's a Ruby on Rails application. So, I will immediately start listing the files in the repository to get a sense of the project structure. This will help me identify key components: likely image upload and storage mechanisms, database models, background job implementations (perhaps using ActiveJob or Sidekiq), and the page deletion process itself. Understanding these pieces and how they interact is crucial to identifying the points where we'll need to insert the cleanup logic. Once I can see where these things are, I'll be in a much better position to assess the current implementation and determine the best approach for the fix. This includes determining where any existing cleanup is done (if any exists) and whether the problem is due to a missing callback, race condition, or a logical flaw in the deletion process.

I need to be able to quickly see what's what, understand dependencies, and ensure efficient build processes and deployments. This initial inventory is going to be the foundation for further analysis, potential refactoring, or optimizing the codebase. module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

require "active_support/core_ext/module/delegation"

# = Active Storage \Attachment
#
# Attachments associate records with blobs. Usually that's a one record-many blobs relationship,
# but it is possible to associate many different records with the same blob. A foreign-key constraint
# on the attachments table prevents blobs from being purged if they’re still attached to any records.
#
# Attachments also have access to all methods from ActiveStorage::Blob.
#
# If you wish to preload attachments or blobs, you can use these scopes:
#
#   # preloads attachments, their corresponding blobs, and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.all.with_attached_avatars
#
#   # preloads blobs and variant records (if using `ActiveStorage.track_variants`)
#   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
class ActiveStorage::Attachment < ActiveStorage::Record
  define_model_callbacks :upload

  after_upload :mirror_blob_later
  after_upload :analyze_blob_later
  after_upload :create_variants

  # Set to true when immediate variants have been processed from local io,
  # so create_variants knows to skip them.
  attr_accessor :immediate_variants_processed

  # Set to true for fresh uploads (io provided), false for existing blobs.
  # Used to determine whether to run :upload callbacks in after_create_commit.
  attr_accessor :pending_upload

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated record.
  belongs_to :record, polymorphic: true, touch: ActiveStorage.touch_attachment_records

  ##
  # :method:
  #
  # Returns the associated ActiveStorage::Blob.
  belongs_to :blob, class_name: "ActiveStorage::Blob", autosave: true, inverse_of: :attachments

  delegate_missing_to :blob
  delegate :signed_id, to: :blob

  after_create_commit :run_upload_callbacks, unless: :pending_upload
  after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later

  ##
  # :singleton-method:
  #
  # Eager load all variant records on an attachment at once.
  #
  #   User.first.avatars.with_all_variant_records
  scope :with_all_variant_records, -> { includes(blob: {
    variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob },
    preview_image_attachment: { blob: { variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob } } }
  }) }

  # Called by Attached::Changes::CreateOne to handle the upload workflow for
  # fresh uploads. Processes immediate variants and analyzes from the local io
  # (avoiding a download round-trip), uploads the blob, then runs the :upload
  # callbacks.
  #
  # For existing blob attachments, the :upload callbacks are run via
  # after_create_commit instead.
  def uploaded(io:)
    blob.local_io = io

    process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
    analyze_blob_from_io(io)

    io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
    blob.upload_without_unfurling(io)

    # Persist analysis metadata if the blob was already saved (happens when
    # upload runs in after_commit, after the blob was saved via autosave).
    blob.save! if blob.persisted? && blob.metadata_changed?

    run_upload_callbacks
  ensure
    blob.local_io = nil
  end

  # Synchronously deletes the attachment and {purges the blob}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge].
  def purge
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge
  end

  # Deletes the attachment and {enqueues a background job}[rdoc-ref:ActiveStorage::Blob#purge_later] to purge the blob.
  def purge_later
    transaction do
      delete
      record.touch if record&.persisted?
    end
    blob&.purge_later
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Variant or ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord
  # instance for the attachment with the set of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   avatar.variant(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   avatar.variant(:thumb).processed.url

  def variant(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.variant(transformations)
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Preview instance for the attachment with the set
  # of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   video.preview(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   video.preview(:thumb).processed.url
  #
  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#preview for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def preview(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.preview(transformations)
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Preview or an ActiveStorage::Variant for the
  # attachment with set of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   avatar.representation(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   avatar.representation(:thumb).processed.url
  #
  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#representation for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def representation(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.representation(transformations)
  end

  private
    def run_upload_callbacks
      run_callbacks(:upload)
    end

    def analyze_blob_later
      blob.analyze_later unless blob.analyzed? || skip_later_analysis?
    end

    def analyze_blob_from_io(io)
      return if blob.analyzed? || skip_later_analysis?

      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      blob.analyze_without_saving
    end

    def skip_later_analysis?
      (analyze_option || ActiveStorage.analyze) == :lazily
    end

    def analyze_option
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.options&.fetch(:analyze, nil)
    end

    def mirror_blob_later
      blob.mirror_later
    end

    def process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
      return unless blob.variable?

      named_variants.each do |_variant_name, named_variant|
        next unless named_variant.process(record) == :immediately

        blob.variant(named_variant.transformations).process_from_io(io)
        io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      end

      self.immediate_variants_processed = true
    end

    def create_variants
      return unless representable?

      immediate_variants = []
      later_variants     = []

      named_variants.each do |_name, named_variant|
        case named_variant.process(record)
        when :immediately
          # Skip if already processed from local io in uploaded()
          immediate_variants << named_variant.transformations unless immediate_variants_processed
        when :later
          later_variants << named_variant.transformations
        end
      end

      ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob.perform_now(blob, variants: immediate_variants, process: :immediately) if immediate_variants.any?
      ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob.perform_later(blob, variants: later_variants, process: :later) if later_variants.any?
    end

    def purge_dependent_blob_later
      blob&.purge_later if dependent == :purge_later
    end

    def dependent
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.options&.fetch(:dependent, nil)
    end

    def named_variants
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.named_variants || {}
    end

    def transformations_by_name(transformations)
      case transformations
      when Symbol
        variant_name = transformations
        named_variants.fetch(variant_name) do
          record_model_name = record.to_model.model_name.name
          raise ArgumentError, "Cannot find variant :#{variant_name} for #{record_model_name}##{name}"
        end.transformations
      else
        transformations
      end
    end
end

  # instance for the attachment with the set of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:

  #   avatar.variant(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url

  #   avatar.variant(:thumb).processed.url

  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def variant(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.variant(transformations)
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Preview instance for the attachment with the set
  # of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   video.preview(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   video.preview(:thumb).processed.url
  #
  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#preview for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.
  def preview(transformations)
    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.preview(transformations)
  end

  # Returns an ActiveStorage::Preview or an ActiveStorage::Variant for the
  # attachment with set of +transformations+ provided.
  # Example:
  #
  #   avatar.representation(resize_to_limit: [100, 100]).processed.url
  #
  # or if you are using pre-defined variants:
  #
  #   avatar.representation(:thumb).processed.url

  # See ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable#representation for more information.
  #
  # Raises an +ArgumentError+ if +transformations+ is a +Symbol+ which is an
  # unknown pre-defined variant of the attachment.

    transformations = transformations_by_name(transformations)
    blob.representation(transformations)
  end

    def run_upload_callbacks
      run_callbacks(:upload)
    end

    def analyze_blob_later
      blob.analyze_later unless blob.analyzed? || skip_later_analysis?
    end

    def analyze_blob_from_io(io)
      return if blob.analyzed? || skip_later_analysis?

      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      blob.analyze_without_saving
    end

    def skip_later_analysis?
      (analyze_option || ActiveStorage.analyze) == :lazily
    end

    def analyze_option
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.options&.fetch(:analyze, nil)
    end

    def mirror_blob_later
      blob.mirror_later
    end

    def process_immediate_variants_from_io(io)
      return unless blob.variable?

      named_variants.each do |_variant_name, named_variant|
        next unless named_variant.process(record) == :immediately

        blob.variant(named_variant.transformations).process_from_io(io)
        io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      end

      self.immediate_variants_processed = true
    end

    def create_variants
      return unless representable?

      immediate_variants = []
      later_variants     = []

      named_variants.each do |_name, named_variant|
        case named_variant.process(record)
        when :immediately
          # Skip if already processed from local io in uploaded()
          immediate_variants << named_variant.transformations unless immediate_variants_processed
        when :later
          later_variants << named_variant.transformations
        end
      end

      ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob.perform_now(blob, variants: immediate_variants, process: :immediately) if immediate_variants.any?
      ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob.perform_later(blob, variants: later_variants, process: :later) if later_variants.any?
    end

    def purge_dependent_blob_later
      blob&.purge_later if dependent == :purge_later
    end

    def dependent
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.options&.fetch(:dependent, nil)
    end

    def named_variants
      record.attachment_reflections[name]&.named_variants || {}
    end

    def transformations_by_name(transformations)
      case transformations
      when Symbol
        variant_name = transformations
        named_variants.fetch(variant_name) do
          record_model_name = record.to_model.model_name.name
          raise ArgumentError, "Cannot find variant :#{variant_name} for #{record_model_name}##{name}"
        end.transformations
      else
        transformations
      end
    end
end

Let's start with `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`. Lines 29-41 are particularly intriguing:

My initial thought is that the `:dependent` option for `has_many_attached` is set to `:destroy`. In `ActiveStorage`:

def has_many_attached(name, dependent: :purge_later, ...)

and in `ActiveStorage::Attachment`:

after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later

def purge_dependent_blob_later
  blob&.purge_later if dependent == :purge_later
end

def dependent

If `ActionText::Markdown` is loaded *before* `ActiveStorage::Attachment`, it's disastrous. Consider a fresh Rails process:

      #   Gallery.where(user: Current.user).with_attached_photos
      #
      # If you need to enable +strict_loading+ to prevent lazy loading of attachments,
      # pass the +:strict_loading+ option. You can do:
      #
      #   class Gallery < ApplicationRecord
      #     has_many_attached :photos, strict_loading: true
      #   end
      #
      # Pass the +analyze:+ option to control when analysis is performed:
      #
      #   class Gallery < ApplicationRecord
      #     has_many_attached :photos, analyze: :immediately
      #   end
      #
      # See +has_one_attached+ for available values and details.
      #
      # Note: Active Storage relies on polymorphic associations, which in turn store class names in the database.
      # When renaming classes that use <tt>has_many</tt>, make sure to also update the class names in the
      # <tt>active_storage_attachments.record_type</tt> polymorphic type column of
      # the corresponding rows.
      def has_many_attached(name, dependent: :purge_later, service: nil, strict_loading: false, analyze: nil)
        Attached::Model.validate_service_configuration(service, self, name) unless service.is_a?(Proc)

        generated_association_methods.class_eval <<-CODE, __FILE__, __LINE__ + 1
          # frozen_string_literal: true
          def #{name}
            @active_storage_attached ||= {}
            @active_storage_attached[:#{name}] ||= ActiveStorage::Attached::Many.new("#{name}", self)
          end

          def #{name}=(attachables)
            attachables = Array(attachables).compact_blank
            pending_uploads = attachment_changes["#{name}"].try(:pending_uploads)

            attachment_changes["#{name}"] = if attachables.none?
              ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::DeleteMany.new("#{name}", self)
            else
              ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::CreateMany.new("#{name}", self, attachables, pending_uploads: pending_uploads)
            end
          end
        CODE

        has_many :"#{name}_attachments", -> { where(name: name) }, as: :record, class_name: "ActiveStorage::Attachment", inverse_of: :record, dependent: :destroy, strict_loading: strict_loading
        has_many :"#{name}_blobs", through: :"#{name}_attachments", class_name: "ActiveStorage::Blob", source: :blob, strict_loading: strict_loading

        scope :"with_attached_#{name}", -> {
          if ActiveStorage.track_variants
            includes("#{name}_attachments": { blob: {
              variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob },
              preview_image_attachment: { blob: { variant_records: { image_attachment: :blob } } }
            } })
          else
            includes("#{name}_attachments": :blob)
          end
        }

        before_validation { attachment_changes[name.to_s]&.analyze }

        after_save { attachment_changes[name.to_s]&.save }

        after_commit(on: %i[ create update ]) { attachment_changes.delete(name.to_s).try(:upload) }

        reflection = ActiveRecord::Reflection.create(
          :has_many_attached,
          name,
          nil,
          { dependent: dependent, service_name: service, analyze: analyze },
          self
        )
        yield reflection if block_given?
        ActiveRecord::Reflection.add_attachment_reflection(self, name, reflection)
      end
    end

    class << self
      def validate_service_configuration(service_name, model_class, association_name) # :nodoc:
        if service_name
          ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(service_name) do
            raise ArgumentError, "Cannot configure service #{service_name.inspect} for #{model_class}##{association_name}"
          end
        else
          validate_global_service_configuration(model_class)
        end
      end

      private
        def validate_global_service_configuration(model_class)
          if model_class.connected? && ActiveStorage::Blob.table_exists? && Rails.configuration.active_storage.service.nil?
            raise RuntimeError, "Missing Active Storage service name. Specify Active Storage service name for config.active_storage.service in config/environments/#{Rails.env}.rb"
          end
        end
    end

    def attachment_changes # :nodoc:
      @attachment_changes ||= {}
    end

    def changed_for_autosave? # :nodoc:
      super || attachment_changes.any?
    end

    def initialize_dup(*) # :nodoc:
      super
      @active_storage_attached = nil
      @attachment_changes = nil
    end

    def reload(*) # :nodoc:
      super.tap { @attachment_changes = nil }
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into ActionText and Leaf Destruction**

Okay, wow, that output was incredible, a real "aha!" moment! I need to document this and then immediately dig deeper. Let's see...

First, that 10-line runner script highlighted a critical issue with `ActiveStorage` integration with `ActionText` and that `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`!  On a fresh boot (or even before `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is loaded), the association is NOT set up correctly! The code cleverly wraps an `include ActionText::Markdown::Uploads` inside `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment`. This likely prevents errors early in the initialization phase when `ActiveStorage` isn't fully configured. But that's not all... it also has a bug! After the attachment *is* loaded, the `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy` declaration means **no** `:purge_later`!  Therefore, those `ActiveStorage::Blob` records and the associated files on disk (in `storage/` or `tmp/storage/`) are *never* deleted! This is a massive resource leak!

Okay, that's one major issue. But wait...

Now, let's explore `Page` edits and destruction. We must examine the interactions of `Leaf`, `Editable`, and `Edit` models.  This `dup_leafable_with_attachments` method looks interesting. I need to understand this whole flow carefully!

Here's the user flow: A user adds an image to a page, which is linked to `ActionText::Markdown` through `ActiveStorage` . Then, when that page is edited, we're making a revision! The current `Leaf` is updated with a *new* `Page` (with the new content), while the original `Page` with the image and content become a `Edit`. However, the code's `has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all` dependency on destroying leaves is a massive oversight. The `delete_all` bypasses any `dependent: :destroy` cascading on the *old* `Page` record, therefore leaving the orphaned `ActionText::Markdown`, `ActiveStorage::Attachment`, and `ActiveStorage::Blob` records!  They're all left to rot in the database and file storage when an edit happens!

Finally, the `trashed!` method is a soft delete, and that means even after we "delete" pages from the UI, we still have that data hanging around.

I need to confirm if there are any background jobs for purging this data. Then, a thorough code review is necessary, checking every occurrence of `destroy`, `delete`, `trash`, `purge`, `uploads`, `Edit`, `Page`, and `Leaf` across the entire codebase!

**Analyzing the Image Deletion Problem**

Okay, first things first, *whoa*! Let's take a deep breath and thoroughly dissect these `grep` results. I need to re-read the problem statement word-for-word, meticulously mapping every detail back to the code. Precision is paramount here.

Okay, let's go again. The core issue is that images embedded in pages aren't being completely removed when the page is deleted. The file persists on disk, and the associated database record remains. The goal? To ensure *complete* removal: "neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app." And crucially, this must occur *after* any background jobs triggered by the deletion have completed.  Uploading and retrieving new images needs to remain unaffected.

Let's break down those phrases with surgical precision:

1.  "Writebook lets an editor drop images straight into a page's markdown body: each image is uploaded once and then referenced inline from the page's content."
2.  "Delete that page, and the image never actually leaves the app — **the file survives on disk, and the record that tracks it survives in the database, forever, even once any background work the deletion sets off has finished running.**"
3.  "Fix it so that **after a page whose markdown has an embedded image is destroyed, and once any background work that destruction triggers has run to completion, neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app.**"
4.  "Uploading a new image into a page's markdown, and then fetching that image back from the URL the app hands you for it, has to keep working exactly as it does today."

Okay, the crucial clue is "neither the image's file nor the record tracking it exists anywhere in the app." In ActiveStorage, that means the following:

*   `ActiveStorage::Attachment` (maps `ActionText::Markdown` <-> `ActiveStorage::Blob`, with `slug`)
*   `ActiveStorage::Blob` (tracks file key, filename, size, checksum, etc.)
*   The actual file on disk. (`ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(blob.key)`)
*   And, if they exist, any `ActiveStorage::VariantRecord`

And what does "after a page whose markdown has an embedded image is destroyed, and once any background work that destruction triggers has run to completion" mean? There are a multitude of potential routes for destruction!

Okay, so I've been tasked with fixing an issue where images embedded in pages aren't truly deleted when the page is removed, and the image file and its database record persist. The prompt specifies this is happening even after background jobs have run, so let's dig into the code and figure out the root cause.

My initial thought is to make sure we don't accidentally break the soft-delete functionality (`trashed!`). It's important to understand *why* the page is being soft-deleted rather than immediately destroyed. It looks like `LeafablesController#destroy` soft-deletes a `Leaf` (which contains a `Page`) and marks its status as "trashed". It doesn't destroy the `Leaf`, `Page`, or the image associated with it. This is confirmed by tests and the app logic.

The crucial problem is: "the file survives on disk, and the record that tracks it survives in the database, forever". The phrase "the record that tracks it" is the key here. It points to `ActiveStorage::Blob` and `ActiveStorage::Attachment` (assuming `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is not lazy-loaded) or `ActiveStorage::Blob` directly if the attachment is destroyed. And "even once any background work the deletion sets off has finished running" strongly suggests that `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` (triggered by `dependent: :purge_later` on the blob) is not being called or is failing.

Now, let's look at every possible scenario for destroying a `Page`, `Leaf`, or `Book`, and what happens to the associated records and files in each case.

The `Page` has a `markdown_body`, which is an `ActionText::Markdown` object. That `ActionText::Markdown` object, has a `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy` declaration in the Rails extension module.
When `page.destroy` is called:
1.  The `ActionText::Markdown` record should be destroyed, which cascades to delete all attachments.
2. In this case, only the `ActionText::Markdown` record is deleted and nothing else happens, the attachment and the blob survive.
3.  Even if that wasn't the case, `dependent: :destroy` on `uploads_attachments` destroys the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` record. But because of the way `after_destroy_commit :purge_dependent_blob_later` runs, the `blob.purge_later` isn't called due to the `:destroy` setting on the `dependent` option of the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` reflection. This means that the `ActiveStorage::Blob` and the image file *survive forever*!

If `dependent: :purge_later` *is* used, then upon destroying `ActiveStorage::Attachment` via `markdown.uploads_attachments`, the `blob.purge_later` is called. It enqueues an `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob`, which deletes the image file from the disk and the blob from the database.

**Deep Dive: Unraveling the Persistent Image Dilemma**

Okay, hold on a minute! Let's hit the brakes and really *digest* everything we've uncovered so far. We've got a lot of information, and we need to approach this with surgical precision. Let's create a solid foundation by meticulously listing and scrutinizing each finding we've made. We'll leave no stone unturned!

First, let's re-familiarize ourselves with the problem statement: the system is failing to fully remove images associated with deleted pages. The images are supposed to be purged from the app after the deletion process completes, but they are not. The images are surviving on the file system and their database records are not being deleted. And the system must continue to work as intended on other features.

Now, let's dissect what we've seen:

**Finding 1: `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` - The Culprit!**

My attention is immediately drawn to the `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` file. The `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy` declaration there is a glaring red flag! This is the core of the problem. Active Storage has *very* specific behavior with `has_many_attached`. It defaults to `:purge_later`. The problem is that someone, likely mistakenly, set this to `:destroy` instead. This is critical.

Here's the sequence we've established: `page.destroy` triggers the deletion of the `markdown_body`, which in turn, should destroy the associated attachments. The `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy` definition, however, is being misinterpreted. It *should* lead to an asynchronous background job (`ActiveStorage::PurgeJob`) being enqueued to remove the image file and associated database record. However, because of the `:destroy` setting, *this job is never enqueued*. It's a classic mix-up! Rails Active Storage is the culprit here. We see the problem in the code:

def purge_dependent_blob_later
  blob&.purge_later if dependent == :purge_later
end

`dependent` is `:destroy`, NOT `:purge_later`! This means that `blob&.purge_later` is *never* called, the job is never enqueued, and the images are left orphaned.

This is where the Rails documentation is important. Rails' own RichText uses the correct behavior as does the cover image in the book model.

This is a notorious Rails ActiveStorage bug.

**Finding 2: The Importance of `ActiveSupport.on_load`!**

Now, before we jump to a solution, we need to think this through. The `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment` block in the same file is crucial.

We need to test the scenario where a `page.destroy` is called *before* the `ActiveStorage::Attachment` is fully loaded to see the full extent of the problem! We need to make sure this isn't masking some other deeper issue. We need to check for side effects with `bin/rails runner` without modifying the DB and within a transaction!

messages.thinking:
**The Solution: A Deep Dive into ActiveStorage and Soft Deletion**

Okay, here's the deal. I've been staring at this code, and it's become crystal clear what's happening and how to fix it. This is a classic ActiveStorage gotcha.

First, the core issue, and it's a BIG one: `has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :destroy`.  This is wrong! ActiveStorage's `dependent: :destroy` with `has_many_attached` *doesn't* actually trigger the blob to be purged, leaving the file and blob record lingering. The solution is simple: Change `dependent: :destroy` to `:purge_later` (or just remove the dependent: option to rely on the default `:purge_later`). This ensures the file and blob are *actually* deleted in the background.

Now, that's not the only problem. The code in `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` is setting up ActiveStorage attachments in a way that creates a nasty load-order dependency. The `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment` block could be skipped if `ActiveStorage::Attachment` isn't loaded before the file. This can lead to the attachments not being properly associated and the purge *never* happening. The fix here is to move the `has_many_attached :uploads` direct into the `ActionText::Markdown` class. This means it *always* gets set up, no matter when ActiveStorage is loaded.

We also have the issue of how leaves, edits, and pages interact with each other. This is complex and we have to consider different scenarios. We need to go through all of them:

*   **Scenario A:** Page destroyed directly, all good.

*   **Scenario B:** Leaf with Page destroyed, also good.

*   **Scenario C:** *This is the key one.* An edited leaf is destroyed. This is a mess: The `delete_all` in `Leaf::Editable` *prevents* cascading deletes. The fix? Change to `dependent: :destroy` in the `has_many :edits` association.  This ensures that when a leaf is deleted, edits and the associated `Page` are all cleaned up, including purging the attachments, bloobs and deletion of the file on disk.  But we have to be *careful* with `leaf.trashed!` as it doesn't destroy the page!

*   **Scenario D:** Destroying `leaf.page` directly. The key here is, *we shouldn't be doing that.* The codebase should always call destroy on the leaf. We'll leave the controller as is because calling the trash does not destroy the page.

*   **Scenario E:** Uploading to a page multiple times and editing. If the leaf is destroyed all edits and pages that the leaf encompasses will be destroyed.

*   **Scenario F:** The Writebook UI (`DELETE /books/:book_id/pages/:id`).  This is where things are tricky because, as we saw when we were tracing earlier, that controller calls `@leaf.trashed!`, which means a soft-delete, not a destroy. **We should NOT change this to a destroy**. The intent here is to soft-delete.  We need to make it clear that the prompt is talking about the case of a hard `destroy`, not the `@leaf.trashed!` because `@leaf.trashed!` should leave everything on disk.

Lastly, and this is crucial, the prompt makes it clear that the image file and blob record *must* be gone after any background jobs have run. With `dependent: :purge_later` on the attachment, and the association fix, that's exactly what will happen.

Alright, let's break this down. **My Immediate Analysis: Destruction in the ActiveStorage Realm**

Okay, hold on a second! This demands immediate attention. We've got a serious potential data persistence issue here, and we need to investigate it *thoroughly* before making any changes. The reproduction script is absolutely the right approach. Let's make sure we have a solid understanding of every single failure mode.

Here's my thought process on what we need to observe.

First, **Scenario 1**: If we upload an image within a `Page`'s markdown, and subsequently destroy the `Page`, we need to confirm that everything cleans up as expected! This involves creating the attachment, verifying its existence in the database and on disk, then triggering destruction and verifying both attachment, blob, and file are gone. We *must* verify that destruction works correctly when the attachment is loaded. The current behavior where the `ActiveStorage::Blob` and the file on disk survive is a major red flag.

Next, **Scenario 2**: Let's consider a scenario where `ActiveStorage::Attachment` hasn't been loaded. If we destroy the page directly, and `ActionText::Markdown` doesn't even have its `uploads` defined, this is another issue.

**Scenario 3** is even more concerning. Let's look at `Leaf` editing and destruction! Let's say that we create a leaf with a page, attach an image, edit the leaf, then destroy the leaf. We need to verify that *all* associated data from previous revisions, including the image files, are properly removed. The fact that `Leaf::Editable`'s `dependent: :delete_all` might bypass the `Edit#destroy` callback and thus prevent proper cleanup of `Page`, `ActionText::Markdown`, `ActiveStorage::Attachment`, `ActiveStorage::Blob`, and the file on disk is a critical concern.

**Scenario 4**: This provides some control and is a good positive test. If we "trash" a `Leaf` and then destroy it, we *expect* everything to be cleaned up as intended, without errors.

Finally, **Scenario 5**: Let's verify file access! Using direct upload via `POST /uploads` and obtaining a `fileUrl` that's accessible, and then performing the destruction, we need to ensure that the image is gone and inaccessible after the destroy. A clean 404 on `GET /u/*slug` is the expected outcome here.

The key is to run the reproduction script, analyze the results carefully, and *then* formulate a solution. No assumptions, no hasty changes. We need to reproduce, understand, and then fix the root cause. This has the potential to lead to a very confusing and challenging problem.

It looks like it's a race condition and a potential, serious, bug.

Scenario 1 illustrates that using `dependent: :destroy` with `has_many_attached` on a model completely *disables* blob purging in that circumstance. This is a critical oversight. It defaults to `dependent: :purge_later`, so using `:destroy` changes that to a no-op! We're leaving files on the disk.

Scenario 2 reinforces this; deleting a `leaf` or `book` exhibits the same issues. It's the same fundamental problem with the `dependent` option being wrongly set.

Scenario 3 is even more concerning. This one involves an edit workflow with `Leaf::Editable`, and the use of `dependent: :delete_all` with `has_many :edits` is causing *orphaned* database records and files! Because destroy on the `Leaf` (or `Book`) uses `delete_all` instead of `destroy`, the associated `Edit` records aren't being properly deleted, and the destruction cascade through `Page`, `ActionText::Markdown`, `ActiveStorage::Attachment`, and `ActiveStorage::Blob` is completely bypassed. I was originally happy with how `leaf` and `book` are fixed with `:destroy` in the edits association.
But, now the thought strikes, how will that work with `leaf.trashed!` + `leaf.destroy`?

**A Deep Dive into ActiveRecord Destruction and Indexing**

Okay, take a deep breath. We just dodged a massive bullet by thoroughly examining `app/models/leaf/searchable.rb`! We almost blindly implemented `dependent: :destroy` on a `has_many` relationship, and that would have led to a catastrophic data loss scenario.

Here's the problem: when we trash a leaf, it creates an "Edit (trash)" that points to the leafable (e.g., a Page). Now, imagine a fresh request where we destroy a book. The critical sequence unfolds like this: We load the leaves, destroy a leaf and its edits. If the `Edit (trash)` destroyed the page BEFORE the leaf's `after_destroy_commit` ran, we'd have a `nil` leafable because it was already destroyed. The `after_destroy_commit :remove_from_search_index` would then attempt to access a non-existent `leafable.searchable_content`, leading to a `Module::DelegationError`.  This would have caused `Book#destroy` to crash whenever it encountered a trashed leaf.

This stems from the fundamental nature of the `Edit (trash)` which shares its leafable with the leaf itself. For "revision" edits, the edit points to an *old* leafable, and it's the edit's responsibility to destroy its association. However, for a "trash" edit, we *don't* want the `Edit` to destroy the leafable prematurely, as the leaf itself still "owns" it. The key is that `Edit (trash)` and the `leaf` both point to the same leafable. So, when the leaf is destroyed, *it* should handle the removal of its own leafable (through `dependent: :destroy` or `destroy_all`) after the `before_destroy` which destroys any associated edits. This ensures that the leafable is still accessible during indexing.

This means we need to ensure that an `Edit` only destroys `leafable` if the `edit` owns the `leafable`. In other words, if it's a revision edit, or if we ensure the edit and the leaf do not share the leafable.

The proper fix is to ensure that `Edit` only destroys the `leafable` if it's a revision edit, to prevent double destruction (once by the `edit` and again by the `leaf`'s own dependent destroy action on its `leafable`).

One last edge case to address is manual editing. To be safe, we added logic in `Edit` to check if `leaf` and the `edit` point to the same leafable.

After destruction, we load the `leafable` into memory before destroying it. This allows `after_destroy_commit :remove_from_search_index, if: :searchable?` to run correctly on `leaf` because `leaf.leafable` is still accessible.

Lastly, there's another crucial fix to be made in the `ActionText::Markdown` module. messages.thinking:
**My Analysis of the Database Destruction Logic**

Okay, so I've been digging into how we're handling the destruction of associated records, particularly with Action Text uploads and polymorphic relationships in the `Leaf` and `Edit` models. `delegated_type` is neat, just passes options to `belongs_to polymorphic: true`. It's crucial, that the right dependencies are being handled during deletion, especially in edge cases like `trash` edits.

I realized the existing `after_destroy` callbacks in `Edit` need tweaking. The current setup was destroying `leafable` too eagerly in some `trash` edit scenarios and would cause issues. With my change, I make sure the correct association destroys the leafable, but only when the `Edit` isn't the current leafable. This ensures the `Leaf` itself destroys the content when it's appropriate, and the `Edit` destroys older versions. I'm making it so that `Edit` only destroys the `leafable` if that leafable isn't the leaf's current version.

I had to look at `update_and_record_edit`. Tricky business. If an image is uploaded and attached to the page's body and that page is updated, we have to make sure every record gets deleted.

I had to trace a few scenarios:
1.  **Direct Destruction:** If I destroy a `Page` directly, it will handle cleaning up its attachments and blobs.
2.  **Leaf Destruction:** If `leaf.destroy` runs, the chain reaction should also be clean: `Edit` destroys `Page` destroys `Markdown` destroys `Attachment` destroys `PurgeJob` and then `Blob` & disk file.
3.  **Potential Problem:** Destroying `leaf.page` directly (instead of `leaf.destroy`) *could* lead to a dangling `Edit` and broken state! This is because there could be no clean up process.

I realized this can happen because `leaf.reload.page.destroy` is possible, but then the edit is still in the database.

I've been thinking about what's going on in the `ActionText::Markdown::Uploads` module. I am wondering if the `dependent: :destroy` used is a problem, which may prevent the attachment's `purge_later` from triggering. I believe I have a safe solution where changing this to `dependent: :purge_later` on the `uploads` association should resolve this. This means when an `ActionText::Markdown` record is destroyed, it sets up an `ActiveStorage::PurgeJob` (which has the task of deleting the associated blobs). I have to test this and make sure nothing breaks! Then, making sure `ActionText::Markdown` *always* includes the module, regardless of when `ActiveStorage::Attachment` loads.

I'm also setting `dependent: :destroy` for the `edits` association on `Leaf` to ensure every edit is destroyed. This triggers the destruction of all related data!

Finally, I made the `after_destroy` changes to `Edit` mentioned earlier to prevent the premature destruction of the current `leafable` during a `trash` edit.

I will also make sure the RuboCop rules are checked, then test all boot environments before and after making these edits.

I believe these adjustments will make the destruction process much more robust and avoid a bunch of potential issues. I am excited to execute these changes and make the tests pass!

messages.content: Let's update `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` to include `ActionText::Markdown::Uploads` in `Rails.application.config.after_initialize` (so `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model` and `ActiveStorage::Reflection` are already registered on `ActiveRecord::Base`, and `uploads` is ALWAYS available on `ActionText::Markdown` immediately after boot without waiting for `ActiveStorage::Attachment` to load).
messages.thinking:
**Eureka! A Deep Dive into Rails Initialization Order**

Wow, this is a breakthrough! I've just uncovered a critical aspect of Rails initialization order, specifically how it interacts with Active Storage and our custom extensions. Look, I see the problem! It's all about the timing of when things are loaded.

I'm looking at how `config/initializers/extensions.rb` modifies the `ActionText::Record` class, which eventually inherits from `ActiveRecord::Base`, and how Active Storage's initializers come into play. It turns out, that critical `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model` module isn't included in `ActiveRecord::Base` *yet* when `extensions.rb` runs because the Active Storage initializers haven't fired. `active_storage.attached` and `active_storage.reflection` initializers run after the application's initializers. Because `extensions.rb` loads our extended class before Active Storage kicks in, it misses the inclusion of that crucial module.

But the solution is elegant. We could try `ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record)` in the extension, but that wouldn't work. By the time that runs, it's already too late.

However, `Rails.application.config.after_initialize` is perfect! That runs *after* all engine initializers, including those in Active Storage, have completed, but *before* a request, console session, or any tests execute. We should be able to cleanly define uploads, reflections, and other features.

Remember that `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` is *not* reloaded on `to_prepare`, and `after_initialize` runs only once at boot. That's why it is the perfect lifecycle hook! 

I'm also considering whether the Active Storage engine's own `config.after_initialize` runs before ours. `active_storage.attached` and `active_storage.reflection` run as initializers, and then `active_storage.configs` has an `after_initialize` block that sets some configs. It's time to confirm the exact order. I'll test it in four distinct environments: a fresh test runner, eager-loaded test, development mode, and production, to be completely certain.

Let's update `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` with `Rails.application.config.after_initialize` and get to testing!

cat <<'EOF' > lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb
module ActionText
  class Markdown < Record
    DEFAULT_RENDERER_OPTIONS = {
      filter_html: false
    }

    DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS = {
      autolink: true,
      highlight: true,
      no_intra_emphasis: true,
      fenced_code_blocks: true,
      lax_spacing: true,
      strikethrough: true,
      tables: true
    }

    mattr_accessor :renderer, default: Redcarpet::Markdown.new(
      Redcarpet::Render::HTML.new(DEFAULT_RENDERER_OPTIONS), DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS)

    belongs_to :record, polymorphic: true, touch: true

    def to_html
      (renderer.try(:call) || renderer).render(content).html_safe
    end
  end
end

module ActionText::Markdown::Uploads
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many_attached :uploads, dependent: :purge_later
  end
end

Rails.application.config.after_initialize do
  ActionText::Markdown.include ActionText::Markdown::Uploads
end

ActiveSupport.run_load_hooks :action_text_markdown, ActionText::Markdown
EOF

**Deep Dive into ActionText and ActiveStorage Initialization**

Okay, so the initial tests are looking good – all three environments (development with reload, test CI with eager load, and production eager load) are booting cleanly with the desired configurations for uploads, dependency, and Sluggable behavior. But I'm feeling like we need to dig a little deeper, poke at some potentially subtle areas.

First, I'm thinking about what happens during a `DemoContent.create_manual` sequence, specifically when a book is destroyed. I need to be *absolutely* certain that every single blob and file associated with the demo content, including the book's cover and the embedded images within its pages, are purged. This warrants a look at `app/models/demo_content.rb` to ensure proper destruction cascading.

Then, there's the more nuanced issue: how the initialization of `ActionText::Markdown` plays with `config/initializers/active_storage.rb` and the `Rails.application.config.after_initialize` hook. I want to be 100% sure there aren't any gotchas. I've reviewed all the initializers in `config/initializers/`, especially `markdown.rb`. It's only setting the renderer and doesn't explicitly touch `.uploads` which is good. There are no other initializers messing with `ActionText::Markdown`. And because `after_initialize` runs before the application finishes initializing, I should be safe. Code running after boot should have the expected behavior.

But, I'm second-guessing myself. What about eager loading in production? Does `eager_load!` run before or after `after_initialize`? I'm going to verify this by checking the Rails internals with `bin/rails runner`. Even if `eager_load!` happens first, `Page` has `has_markdown :body` – that defines `has_one :markdown_body` and doesn't directly call `.uploads`, so it should be fine. However, let's explore if `ActionText::Markdown.attachment_reflections` would still work if a subclass runs or with `ActiveSupport.on_load :action_text_markdown`.

Next thought: What if someone uses `ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_attached)`? Does such a hook even exist? No. ActiveStorage only has a few other options. And then I remember: why did `ActionText::Markdown.include ActionText::Markdown::Uploads` fail earlier? The only reason for the failure was that `config/initializers/extensions.rb` ran BEFORE `ActiveStorage::Engine`'s `initializer "active_storage.attached"`!

And the burning question: WHY did `extensions.rb` run first?! In Rails, the initializer order dictates that loading `config/initializers/*` happens AFTER engine initializers... WAIT NO! Why did `extensions.rb` fail?! I need to investigate using `bin/rails runner` why `active_storage.attached` hadn't run yet! There's a fundamental issue I need to understand here.

**Eureka! The Table Holds the Key!**

AHAHAHAHA! This table... it *explains everything* with such elegant mathematical clarity! I see it now; the boot sequence reveals the critical path!

First, at step 216 (`Writebook::Application#load_config_initializers`), we execute `config/initializers/extensions.rb`, which includes `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb`. Crucially, at this point, neither `active_storage.attached` nor `active_storage.reflection` have yet run! This perfectly explains the initial problem the author faced! They couldn't directly call `has_many_attached` within `action_text_markdown.rb` because the necessary Active Storage hooks weren't available. They tried `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment`, but this inadvertently delayed the attachment of `uploads` until something else triggered the loading of `ActiveStorage::Attachment`. A clever, but ultimately flawed, attempt.

Then, at steps 244 and 248, `ActiveStorage::Engine` kicks in, adding `ActiveStorage::Attached::Model` (and therefore `has_many_attached`) and `ActiveStorage::Reflection` to `ActiveRecord::Base`.

The real genius of this solution lies in step 300, `Writebook::Application#finisher_hook`, where we use `config.after_initialize`. This is brilliant because:

*   It executes *after* `active_storage.attached`, `active_storage.reflection`, and the configuration.
*   It runs unconditionally in *every* environment, regardless of eager loading.
*   It executes *only once* at boot – no re-defining of callbacks on development code reloads.
*   It avoids forcing `ActiveStorage::Attachment` to load at boot in lazy-loading scenarios. If the attachment is already loaded, `ActiveStorage::Sluggable` is included by the already loaded `ActiveSupport.on_load :active_storage_attachment`.

Wait! A quick comparison of step 299 (`eager_load!`) and step 300 (`finisher_hook` / `after_initialize`) seals the deal! Is there ANY code that, during eager loading, *needs* `ActionText::Markdown#uploads`? No! Models simply define associations during eager loading.

Furthermore, consider `config.to_prepare`. While it runs after `finisher_hook`, it *also* runs on every development reload. We want `after_initialize` because `lib/rails_ext/action_text_markdown.rb` *isn't* reloaded on dev reloads! Calling `has_many_attached` once in `after_initialize` avoids unnecessary callback redefinitions on every development reload!

---

Okay, now it's time to **check the entire test suite** and write **thorough tests** to ensure we've got a robust solution! Let's start with a full run of the existing test suite to ensure everything still passes!

messages.thinking:
**Thoroughly Examining Edge Cases Before Testing**

Okay, before I dive into writing these new tests, I need to be absolutely certain I've covered some critical edge cases. I can see the potential pitfalls here, so let's carefully consider each scenario.

First, I need to simulate a *cross-process* fresh boot destroy *without* ever loading `ActiveStorage::Attachment` first. The idea is to have one process create a Page, upload an image, and save everything. Then, a completely new process, with `eager_load = false`, will attempt to destroy that Page (and all associated assets) without having previously interacted with any of the `ActiveStorage` objects. I need to verify that the attachment, blob, and the actual file on disk are all properly cleaned up. This feels like a classic race condition and could easily break if not handled correctly.

Next, I need to understand what happens with a `Picture` leaf that has been edited before it's destroyed, let's trace this out. I have to make sure that the system correctly handles the duplicate images after being edited. It starts with `leaves(:reading_picture)` and `Picture #1`, `Attachment #1`, and `Blob #1`. Then the edits are made. The `dup_leafable_with_attachments` creates `Picture #2` -> `Attachment #2` and we use the SAME `Blob #1`. I also have to consider the `Edit #1` pointing to `Picture #1` (`Attachment #1` -> `Blob #1`) and that `Leaf` is pointing to `Picture #2` (`Attachment #2` -> `Blob #1`). I then perform the destroy, `perform_enqueued_jobs { leaves(:reading_picture).destroy }`. I need to be sure that the old relationships are deleted. The transaction commits and `PurgeJob` should correctly run for `Blob #1`, with no attachments left, and finally destroy `Blob #1` and the file. Previously, `Attachment #1` could have lingered and kept the file from being purged.

Similarly, I need to test what happens when a `Picture` leaf has its image *replaced* via an `edit` before destruction. In this scenario, `Edit #1` will have `Picture #1` which points to `Blob #1`. The `Leaf` will have `Picture #2` -> `Blob #2`. Then `leaf.destroy` should correctly destroy BOTH `Picture #1` and `Picture #2`, which should subsequently destroy BOTH `Blob #1` and `Blob #2`, and of course the files on disk!

Then, I need to examine how a `Page` with multiple embedded images behaves during destruction, and what happens when a `Page` has *no* embedded images. I anticipate that for multiple images, all attachments, blobs, and disk files will be destroyed. For pages without images, I expect `page.destroy` to work cleanly without any purge jobs being enqueued.

Finally, I need to consider a scenario involving `DemoContent.create_manual` and then `book.destroy`. Here I need to test BOTH the cross-process fresh boot destroy *and* the interplay of `DemoContent` and `Picture` with edits. This will be a more comprehensive integration test.

page = Page.create!(body: "Cross-process test")

page.body.uploads.attach(io: File.open(file_path), filename: "reading.webp", content_type: "image/webp")
page.body.save!
att = page.body.uploads.attachments.last

ActiveJob::Base.queue_adapter = :test

puts \"  attachment exists? \#{ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(att_id)}\"
puts \"  blob exists?       \#{ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob_id)}\"
puts \"  file on disk?      \#{ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(blob_key)}\"
"

require "test_helper"

class ActionText::Markdown::UploadsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  test "attach a file" do
    assert_changes -> { ActiveStorage::Attachment.count }, 1 do
      post action_text_markdown_uploads_url, params: {
        record_gid: pages(:welcome).to_signed_global_id.to_s,
        attribute_name: "body",
        file: fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
      }, as: :xhr
    end

    assert_response :success

    # Uploads should use relative URLs, to allow for future hostname changes
    assert JSON.parse(response.body)["fileUrl"].start_with?("/")
  end

  test "view attached file" do
    markdown = pages(:welcome).body.tap(&:save!)
    markdown.uploads.attach fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")

    attachment = pages(:welcome).body.uploads.last

    get action_text_markdown_upload_url(slug: attachment.slug)

    assert_response :redirect
    assert_match /\/rails\/active_storage\/.*\/reading\.webp/, @response.redirect_url
  end

  test "uploaded image can be fetched and is purged when page is destroyed" do
    post action_text_markdown_uploads_path, params: {
      record_gid: pages(:welcome).to_signed_global_id.to_s,
      attribute_name: "body",
      file: fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
    }, as: :xhr

    assert_response :created
    file_url = JSON.parse(response.body)["fileUrl"]

    get file_url
    assert_response :redirect
    get response.location
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal file_fixture("reading.webp").binread, response.body

    attachment = pages(:welcome).body.uploads.attachments.last
    blob = attachment.blob
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(blob.key)

    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      pages(:welcome).destroy
    end

    assert_not ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(attachment.id)
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(blob.key)

    get file_url
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "uploaded image embedded via page update is purged when leaf is destroyed" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)

    post action_text_markdown_uploads_path, params: {
      record_gid: leaf.page.to_signed_global_id.to_s,
      attribute_name: "body",
      file: fixture_file_upload("reading.webp", "image/webp")
    }, as: :xhr

    assert_response :created
    file_url = JSON.parse(response.body)["fileUrl"]

    attachment = leaf.page.body.uploads.attachments.last
    blob = attachment.blob

    put leafable_path(leaf), params: {
      leaf: { title: leaf.title },
      page: { body: "Here is an image: ![reading](#{file_url})" }
    }
    assert_response :no_content

    get file_url
    assert_response :redirect
    get response.location
    assert_response :ok

    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      leaf.reload.destroy
    end

    assert_not ActiveStorage::Attachment.exists?(attachment.id)
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.exists?(blob.id)
    assert_not ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(blob.key)

    get file_url
    assert_response :not_found
  end
end
